title: Restore two borrowed dirty buffers across the R439 packet window
body:
PR2448 leaves its fresh-copy/disposal contract separate from dirty ancilla admission. This result gives a conditional replacement for the exact 313-event R439 window: exchange each packet into one of two borrowed dirty buffers, route and update it, return the route, then exchange back. Each event restores its source and both buffers; the snapshot remains immutable throughout.

The complete outer bill is 1,232 route calls, 1,232 packet exchanges and 4,009 packet XOR passes. The outer adapter uses no blank payload records or CLEAR/disposal operations. It requires temporary exchange of original source/target packets, arbitrary parked-value preservation by every route child, and separately supplied headers, control storage and route-private scratch. This is a more expensive route bill than the predecessor's 929-route fresh-copy implementation. It is not a uniform GL64 compiler, complete reversible supplier, global helper admission or new kappa.

The package includes an arbitrary correlated-payload proof and a source-bound GL2(Z/9) replay. It checks all 431,568 family records, including 422,577 unowned records, with 431,811 independent formal input atoms and an endpoint oracle based on full-ring multiplication. Forward and reversed words pass. Six mutations reject the dirty-copy shortcut, missing restoration, omitted carries, a forbidden snapshot write attempt and wrong chronological tap placement.

Validation: native CPython 3.12.7 registered normal and optimized commands pass. A separate AI reviewer using the bundled CPython 3.12.14 inspected the proof, implementation and retained source contracts, passed the optimized replay and read-only Git-free export, and confirmed all ten retained/live source corruption controls fail before import and a modified cost receipt fails after replay. No material issue was found in the stated conditional contract. No human review, complete selected supplier replay or hosted CI pass is claimed.

Only `research/r439-dirty-packet-adapter` is added. PR2448 is pinned at `76311b90337a04dd811877d101c86ff8ecd65904`; seven consumed source/contract files retain exact SHA256 and Git blob bindings. The route compiler and PR2407-derived source-window constructor are reused explicitly, with a separate baseline endpoint. Canonical main was refreshed at the start, pivot and before submission and remains `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. Selected and frozen evidence are unchanged.

Final overlap refresh at 2026-10-15 12:24:54 UTC covered 679 open PRs and 1,197 discussion/comment/reply records with complete pagination and no warnings. The four dirty-packet/exchange terms returned only this local package. The search covers titles, bodies, discussions and local notes, not every code diff; no match is not proof of novelty.

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-dirty-packet-adapter
```

Credit Ross Richardson's PR2448/2407/2437 and Jose Manuel's PR2195 for the retained window and packet contracts. The three-XOR reversible exchange is standard; this contribution is the changed ownership contract, chronological source binding and complete local invoice. Concurrent PR2475 stages a whole BIT call using fresh private copies; it leaves a different allocation contract and does not supply this two-bank per-event dirty restoration. Prepared for ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Advance claim and eventual status: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2448#issuecomment-6191586623.
